hypothesis: R232 is the closest composite candidate (11/12 gates, full +6.87%, recent 12m +17.26%) and uses 10 positions, unlike the concentrated 5-position R238. Before attempting to fix R232's G1 failure, this round audits whether its P&L is diversified across symbols and industries. If R232 is also dominated by one stock, the entire SGA/OCF/gross-margin family is too narrow and should be abandoned rather than retuned.

execution.universe: historical non-financial HS300 membership; daily snapshots from 2022

gates.C1: at least 30 distinct symbols are traded across the full period
gates.C2: the single largest symbol's share of net P&L is at most 25%
gates.C3: the top three symbols' share of net P&L is at most 55%
gates.C4: the top five symbols' share of net P&L is at most 75%
gates.C5: at least 8 distinct symbols have positive P&L in the validation segment
gates.C6: the largest industry's share of gross profit is at most 45%
gates.C7: the single largest symbol loss is at most 20% of gross profit in absolute value

decision_rule: All C gates must pass. A failure means R232's P&L is too concentrated to justify further tuning; the factor family should be abandoned and the next round should move to a different data dimension.
known_limitations: Trade P&L amounts from two segments each start from 1,000,000 notional, so shares are contribution-share diagnostics, not compounded-return decomposition.
Industry classification is a current snapshot, not historical PIT.
The audit describes concentration, not causality.
